quote.text: Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I shall move the world.
quote.author: Archimedes, as reported by Pappus of Alexandria (Synagoge, c. 340 AD)

stories.headline: Israel Bombs a Syrian Runway to Keep Turkey Off It
stories.dek: Eight strikes on an airbase near Aleppo, eleven days after a new Saudi–Pakistan–Turkey defence pact — and this time Washington rebuked Israel, not the men it hit. Two American allies are now carving the same country.

stories.headline: The Chips Finally Cross the Border — and Beijing Grabs the Throttle
stories.dek: After seven months in limbo, physical H200s are landing on the mainland. But the firms have taken barely a tenth of what Washington licensed them to buy — because the hand on the tap is now the NDRC, steering the money toward Huawei instead.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · Home Theatre — The Invitation
stories.headline: The Room Is the Machine, and the Box Is Just the Box
stories.dek: Building a dedicated cinema at home is the rare hobby where the most expensive thing you can buy — the projector — is not the thing that decides how good it looks. The lever is the room, the calibration and the bass. This is a hobby that punishes the shortcut.

stories.headline: Sunday's Rally Reaches for the Cost of Raising a Child
stories.dek: The government has pre-trailed a "fresh look" at childcare fees and the load on young families. What Prime Minister Wong lays down on Sunday is the structural layer above Budget's one-off vouchers — and the thing the room is actually waiting for.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 5 · Ski Gadgets & On-Mountain Electronics
stories.headline: The Mountain Sells You Rentals and Calls Them Gear
stories.dek: The hardest category this desk has met: buy-once meets a battery, a firmware update and a retirement date. The honest answer is a sorting job — what lasts a decade, what you replace on a schedule, and what is a subscription wearing a jacket.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The Compact Cinema Camera
stories.headline: GoPro Stops Making Action Cams and Builds a Pocket Cinema Rig
stories.dek: The Mission 1 Pro is a genuine departure: a one-inch, fifty-megapixel sensor shooting 8K in a body you still clip to a bag. The reviews call it GoPro's best camera in years — and its most un-GoPro.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Indie Bench
stories.headline: A Regatta Watch for a Race That Never Happened
stories.dek: Albishorn builds "imaginary vintage" — faithful reissues of watches that never existed. Its Marinagraph adds two quieter colourways and a genuinely patented trick: a ten-minute countdown that snaps back to zero.

stories.headline: A Bourdain Origin Story Opens Wide on a Perfect Score
stories.dek: A24's "Tony" arrives in cinemas today with a hundred-per-cent tally and Dominic Sessa as a young Anthony Bourdain. And Chelsea Wolfe drops her ninth record the same day, casting off the doom for something almost tender.

stories.headline: The Lever You're Looking For Is the Pillow, Not the Phone
stories.dek: A new analysis of thousands of ten-to-thirteen-year-olds finds sleep — not screen time — is what carries mental-health strain into school grades. For a child starting secondary one on an earlier alarm, that reorders the whole worry list.

stories.headline: The Government Reached In and Set the Price of Its Own Debt
stories.dek: The thirty-year touched a nineteen-year high, so the Treasury doubled its buybacks and pushed it back down. The long end is now administered as much as it is traded — and the dollar noticed first.

stories.headline: The Smallest Lever That Still Moves the Needle Is Five Minutes
stories.dek: A review of eleven trials finds "exercise snacks" — sub-five-minute bouts, twice a day — genuinely lift cardiorespiratory fitness in the sedentary. Benefits showed up at as little as four and a half minutes a week. The dose is almost embarrassingly small.

stories.headline: A Grand Prix With Real Points, and a Region Hosting the Asian Games
The Country Backing Away From Moscow Is Walking Into Its Apps
stories.dek: Astana has spent four years distancing itself from the Kremlin — refusing to endorse the war, taking in those who fled it. And in the same four years, the phone in every Kazakh pocket has drifted the other way, into Russia's Yandex, one convenient tap at a time.
